column1: What does "japa" mean in Nigerian usage?
column2: Emigrating abroad, especially young people and professionals leaving Nigeria for opportunities elsewhere.

column1: How many doctors left Nigeria in 2024?
column2: 3,974, a 10-year high (compared with 688 in 2015), per Federal Ministry of Health data.

column1: How many nurses and midwives left Nigeria in 2024?
column2: Over 23,000; top destinations were the US (8,613), UK (7,463) and Canada (5,603).

column1: What share of Nigerians want to migrate, according to the NBS 2023/24 survey?
column2: About 1 in 4 overall, and 34.5% of those aged 20–30.

column1: What is the difference between the official 6.5% and the civil-society 53% youth unemployment figures?
column2: The NBS 6.5% (ages 15–24, Q2 2024) uses the ILO method counting even one hour of work a week; the 53% (Plan International/ActionAid) is a broader estimate. Neither captures underemployment.

column1: Why does the official unemployment rate feel too low to many Nigerians?
column2: It counts anyone working an hour a week and misses underemployment; 93% of workers are in informal employment.

column1: How should callers answer Peter Obi's "80% youth unemployment" claim?
column2: The ActionAid/Plan International report he cites actually put the rate at 53%, and it is a civil-society estimate, not an NBS figure.

column1: What has the student loan scheme (NELFUND) disbursed?
column2: ₦375.28 billion across 1,675,474 loans, covering tuition paid to institutions and upkeep paid to students (portal opened 24 May 2024).

column1: How should callers answer "the student loan money was stolen"?
column2: The ICPC corrected its ₦71.2bn statement (the word "NOT" was omitted) and found no fraud; the probe followed NELFUND's own petition. Admit institution deductions and upkeep delays.

column1: What is the 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme's record?
column2: The pilot trained 135,000+ people in three cohorts, with 1.8 million in the pipeline from January 2026; only 19% of Cohort 1 completed.

column1: Give an example of 3MTT leading to work.
column2: Cohort 1 fellows were placed in internships paying ₦100,000 a month, and the government is arranging jobs for about 117,000 fellows through outsourcing firms.

column1: What is the Labour Employment and Empowerment Programme (LEEP)?
column2: A programme launched 15 April 2025 targeting 2.5 million jobs in two years; no job placements had been recorded by mid-2025.

column1: What is the National Policy on Health Workforce Migration?
column2: A policy approved on 12 August 2024 to retain health workers, set ethical recruitment deals and reintegrate returnees; the retirement age rose to 65 (70 for consultants) in February 2025.

column1: How has inflation changed since its peak?
column2: It fell from 33.88% in October 2024 to 14.63% in September 2026 (NBS), so prices are rising more slowly.

column1: Why is "japa" not a problem created by this administration?
column2: It predates it: polls found 69% of young Nigerians wanted to leave in 2022, before Tinubu took office.

column1: Give an example of a beneficiary story callers can use.
column2: UNILAG student Migwe Obinna Nicholas said he was "on the verge of dropping out" before NELFUND paid his fees; Olabisi Onabanjo University's leave-of-absence requests fell from about 3,000 a year to zero.

column1: Which youth counter-arguments are strong and which are weak?
column2: Strong: falling inflation and student loans. Mixed: jobs programmes and unemployment figures. Weak: health-worker emigration and "jobless growth".

column1: How should callers handle the "japa is modern-day slavery" remark?
column2: Don't defend or repeat it; pivot to the 2024 health-workforce policy for returnees and the $21.8bn diaspora remittances in 2025.

column1: Why shouldn't callers say japa is good because of remittances?
column2: It sounds dismissive to families who have lost people to emigration.

column1: Why shouldn't the Youth Investment Fund be presented as a Tinubu programme?
column2: It began in 2020, before his administration.

column1: How should callers respond to Atiku's claim that youths are selling kidneys?
column2: Don't argue the point, since no data links organ sales to policy; acknowledge the hardship and cite falling inflation (33.88% to 14.63%).
